Leipzig, Germany · 2–5 June 2026

The Forum

Two working days that turned the experience of very different organisations into one shared voice on the future of Erasmus+.

The Erasmus+ Future Forum was coordinated by Dreaming OPEnly e.V., part of garagErasmus, and financed by ESAA. It brought together representatives of international networks, associations, education professionals and trainers active across the Erasmus+ Programme.

The aim was simple and ambitious: to create a structured, representative space for reflection and coordination, and to influence the next Erasmus+ (2028–2034) directly, as the people who deliver it.

What happened in the room

How it worked

→

We mapped the field

We mapped the networks active within Erasmus+ — who does what, and where the overlaps and gaps are.

→

Eight working sessions

Facilitated sessions explored the strengths and gaps of the current programme, and the needs, risks and opportunities for 2028–2034.

→

We co-wrote the paper

Collaborative writing turned field experience into one position paper, authored together by every network present.

→

A shared voice

The Forum created a space for networks and associations to meet, recognise common challenges and begin building a shared voice for the future of Erasmus+.

Who is in the room

Who was there

The Forum brought together twenty-two organisations, international Erasmus+ networks, local Leipzig associations and public authorities; each speaking for the wider community behind it.
